ground_truth.description: The helpers are imported by the bare top-level module name `from _workflow_helpers import ...`. Under root-level pytest with `--import-mode=importlib` (the exact scenario the module docstring cites), this registers `sys.modules['_workflow_helpers']` as a non-namespaced top-level name. If any other subproject also has a `_workflow_helpers.py`, this reintroduces the same cross-subproject module collision the extraction was meant to avoid, and bare-name resolution of a sibling module is not guaranteed without the tests dir on sys.path, risking a ModuleNotFoundError at collection time in root-level runs.

`_make_status_setting_steward` resolves pending L0 escalations without asserting any exist (unlike `_make_resolving_steward`, which asserts `pending`). If the queue has no pending L0 for the task, the loop silently no-ops and the steward still sets `final_status`, potentially masking a setup regression where the escalation path was never exercised.

The rewritten 'Static Protocol conformance checks' header comment gives a false rationale: it says the block stays at the bottom of the file so the FakeScheduler import is resolved before pyright evaluates the checks, then concedes top placement would still work; pyright does not depend on statement order for module-level imports. It also contains reviewer-directed prose ('avoids unnecessary diff noise') and describes a block that actually sits ~1,100 lines further down (if TYPE_CHECKING at line 5091).

After FakeScheduler moved to _workflow_helpers.py, its static conformance check `_fake_scheduler_conforms: _SchedulerLike = FakeScheduler()` remains in test_workflow_e2e.py's TYPE_CHECKING block, so the shared helper module gives no sign that the fake is contract-checked against _SchedulerLike.

The new, unrequested test_workflow_helpers.py adds tests of little value: test_imports_resolve duplicates what module-level imports in the two consumer test files already enforce at collection, and the FakeMcp/FakeBriefing smoke tests echo the fakes' canned literals. Its docstring says the 5 helpers 'behave as expected', yet the only helpers with logic, _make_resolving_steward and _make_status_setting_steward, have no tests.

Every test in test_workflow_helpers.py imports _workflow_helpers inside the function with `# noqa: PLC0415`. There is no cycle or ordering reason for a function-local import, and PLC is not in orchestrator's ruff select list, so the suppressions are inert noise.

FakeScheduler moved to _workflow_helpers.py, but its existing tests (TestFakeSchedulerGetStatus) stayed in test_workflow_e2e.py while the new test_fake_scheduler_smoke repeats the same get_status-after-two-sets behaviour, so the fake's tests now have two homes.

_make_resolving_steward and _make_status_setting_steward keep a module-private leading underscore although they are now the exported API of a shared helper module imported by test_workflow_e2e.py, test_workflow_status_on_resume.py and test_workflow_helpers.py.

The moved _make_resolving_steward docstring says it is 'Used by TestMarkBlockedFalseDoneGuard tests' and refers to _mark_blocked's `if not remaining:` branch, which is consumer-specific context from test_workflow_e2e.py that no longer reads correctly in a shared helper module.

The new module docstrings cite task history instead of tracked sources: _workflow_helpers.py says 'See task 977 for convention rationale' (the convention is documented in tests/scripts/test_pytest_workspace_collection.py) and test_workflow_helpers.py says it verifies behaviour 'after extraction from test_workflow_e2e.py (task 1195)'.

Only the two cross-imported steward factories moved to _workflow_helpers.py; the sibling fake-steward factories (_make_dismissing_steward, _make_l1_escalating_steward, _make_done_setting_steward) remain in the 5,096-line test_workflow_e2e.py, so the factory family now lives in two files with no stated partition rule.

_workflow_helpers.py imports EscalationQueue at runtime although, under `from __future__ import annotations`, it is used only in annotations; it could sit under TYPE_CHECKING. The cost is negligible because every consumer already imports escalation.queue.

task.title: Extract shared test fixtures from test_workflow_e2e.py to a helpers module
task.description:
orchestrator/tests/test_workflow_status_on_resume.py imports `FakeBriefing`, `FakeMcp`, `FakeScheduler`, `_make_resolving_steward`, and `_make_status_setting_steward` directly from the sibling test module `test_workflow_e2e`. Cross-test imports create fragile coupling — if `test_workflow_e2e` collection fails or its helpers move, `test_workflow_status_on_resume` silently breaks. The reorder in task 1191 also moved this import ahead of first-party orchestrator imports, against convention.

Extract these helpers into a shared module — either `orchestrator/tests/conftest.py` (for fixture-style helpers) or a `orchestrator/tests/_helpers.py` / `orchestrator/tests/_workflow_helpers.py` module — and import from there in both files. Note convention from task 977: prefer extracting to uniquely-named sibling modules over conftest when the helpers don't fit the fixture model. Restore correct first-party-last import grouping in test_workflow_status_on_resume.py after extraction.
